title: Neural Retrievers are Biased Towards LLM-Generated Content

problem.claim: IR systems must retrieve from collections containing both human-written and LLM-generated documents.

gap.claim: The influence of LLM-generated documents on IR systems was pressing and still unexplored.

contributions.claim: Neural retrieval models tend to rank LLM-generated documents higher than human-written documents.
LLM-generated texts exhibit more focused semantics with less noise, which may make semantic matching easier for neural retrieval models.
The work proposes a plug-and-play debiased constraint for the optimization objective to mitigate source bias.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Quantitative evaluation was conducted in scenarios involving both human-written and LLM-generated texts.
The observed source bias extends from first-stage neural retrievers to second-stage neural re-rankers.
Experimental results reportedly show that the proposed debiased constraint is effective.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs generate large amounts of human-like text, creating mixed-origin document collections for IR systems.
The effect of LLM-generated documents on IR systems is identified as an unexplored question.
The work quantitatively evaluates IR models on collections containing human-written and LLM-generated texts.
Neural retrievers and re-rankers show source bias toward LLM-generated content, associated with its more focused semantics and lower noise.
A plug-and-play debiased optimization constraint is proposed, with reported effective experimental results, alongside new benchmarks for future exploration.

source_observation.claim: Neural retrieval models tend to rank LLM-generated documents higher, and the bias extends to neural re-rankers.

interpretation.claim: Document-generation source can systematically affect neural retrieval rankings across multiple retrieval stages.

application.claim: Evaluate retrieval systems for source-dependent ranking effects whenever indexed collections mix human- and machine-generated content.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that the bias occurs for every neural retrieval model, dataset, or deployment setting.

source_observation.claim: The analysis associates the bias with more focused semantics and less noise in LLM-generated texts.

interpretation.claim: Text characteristics that simplify semantic matching may create systematic retrieval preferences.

application.claim: Use source-aware diagnostics and debiasing objectives when content-style differences may influence semantic matching.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which text-compression measures or content conditions support this interpretation.

unknowns: The evaluated retrieval models, datasets, metrics, and experimental conditions are unspecified.
The construction and scope of the two benchmarks are unspecified.
The formulation and optimization details of the debiased constraint are unspecified.
The magnitude and statistical strength of the reported bias and mitigation effect are unspecified.
